transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since they changed everything at school, I feel like I’m not handling it well at all and my reactions to the stress are taking over my life. I've always been able to manage my work, but lately, I just feel completely overwhelmed by how much this is affecting me.
Can you describe how you've been feeling when you say 'overwhelmed' - is it more like a constant worry, fear, or a feeling of sadness that's been bothering you?

It’s really a mix of both intense worry and sadness, and it feels like I’m on a constant emotional roller coaster. I find myself crying in my car in the parking lot because I dread walking into the classroom, and then I lie awake at night replaying test scores and curriculum scripts in my head.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you used to enjoy doing, such as hobbies or spending time with friends, since you've been feeling this way?

Yes, I've completely stopped doing things I used to love, like my watercolor painting and salsa dancing nights. I'm just so drained and irritable that I've been skipping family get-togethers and barely even talk to my husband in the evenings.

Can you tell me more about what's been going on with your painting and dancing - is it that you've lost interest in them altogether, or is it more that you just don't have the energy to do them anymore?

It’s really a mix of both. I’ve stopped enjoying my watercolor sessions and salsa nights, which used to bring me so much joy, and I also feel completely drained by the end of the day from the constant stress and late-night lesson planning, leaving me with absolutely no energy to do them.
Can you think of any activities or things that still bring you some joy or pleasure, even if it's just a little, despite everything else going on?

Honestly, nothing really brings me joy right now. I used to absolutely love watercolor painting and going to salsa dancing nights, but lately, I have completely stopped enjoying them and don't even have the energy or desire to do them anymore because of the overwhelming stress from school.

You mentioned that the changes at school triggered these feelings, can you tell me more about how you think you would feel if the school situation were to resolve itself or go back to how it was before?

If they would just ease up on these new test-score demands or let me go back to the style of teaching I used to do, I really believe I could finally calm down. I feel like I would be able to escape this constant state of work-related tension and feel like myself again.

Do you think you would still experience these feelings of worry and sadness if you were no longer in this stressful school situation, or do you feel like they would significantly improve or disappear?

I am confident that my feelings would significantly improve if the school situation changed. If they eased up on the test-score demands or let me return to my previous style of teaching, I know I could finally calm down. I really believe I would be able to shake off this constant state of work-related tension.

If the school situation were to completely resolve itself and go back to how it was before, do you think you would still experience any symptoms of worry, sadness, or loss of interest in activities, or would they completely disappear?

I am convinced they would completely disappear, as all of this distress is tied directly to what has been happening at school. If the demands eased up or I could go back to my old classroom, I know I would finally calm down and feel like myself again.

If the school situation were to completely resolve itself and you were able to go back to teaching the way you used to, how long do you think it would take for you to start feeling like yourself again and enjoying the things you used to enjoy?

I honestly think it would happen pretty quickly, probably within a few months of that constant work-related tension finally lifting. Once I could go back to the style of teaching I love, I know I would finally calm down and get my old self back.
